name: New Colour
summary: Colour photography of the plain American scene: a car park, a kitchen, a tricycle. Saturated dye-transfer and slide colour carries the picture, and the composition looks casual and exact at the same time.

philosophy.core_thesis: Colour is the subject and not a decoration, and the everyday world is rich enough to need no drama.
design_principles: Choose the subject for its colour relationships, and keep to three or four dominant hues in the frame.
Shoot on slide or dye-transfer stock at ISO 25 to 64 for deep, saturated colour with a fine grain.
Use a 35mm to 50mm lens at f/5.6 to f/11 and a low or oblique viewpoint at 1 to 3m.
Accept the light as found: midday sun, shop windows and fluorescent tubes, and let the mixed colour casts show.
Keep the composition casual but exact: put the subject off centre, with a strong colour mass in balance.
Show the ordinary: cars, diners, kitchens and car parks, with no hero and no punchline.
anti_patterns: Black and white conversion or desaturated grading
Golden hour glow and a colour cast added in the lab
Centred hero subjects with a clear message
Shallow depth of field that blurs the colour of the background
A uniform filter look over the whole frame

composition.framing: Square or 3:2 frame, with the subject cropped slightly by the edge and a large colour field in the frame.
composition.viewpoint: Low, tilted or at eye height, 1 to 3m from the subject; the camera looks at the thing as an equal.
composition.geometry: Colour blocks and horizon lines; a single diagonal of a car or a cable.
composition.subject_placement: Off centre, with a colour mass of 30–40% of the frame as a counterweight.

principles.rule: Set 60% in one dominant hue, 30% in its neighbour and 10% in an accent, with 3 to 4 hues in all.
Put the subject within 0.05 of 0.33 or 0.67 of the width.
Crop the subject by 5–10% at one edge.
Use 2 planes only: a near object at 1–3m and a flat background at 6m or more.

light.quality: Found light, as it is: hard sun or the flat light of a shop and a kitchen.
light.direction: Any; often overhead sun for saturated colour with short shadows.

lens_and_camera.format: 35mm slide or colour negative; 8×10 in for dye-transfer prints
lens_and_camera.focus: Sharp on the subject with the background held to a depth of 3m to infinity.

colour_and_grade.treatment: Deep, dense dye colours with clean whites: reds and cyans are the strongest, and shadows keep a rich colour.
grade_recipe: Set the white point at 94% and the black point at 3%, with 18% grey at the midpoint.
Raise saturation by +25% and vibrance by +10%.
Push red hue by +4° and cyan by −3° to match dye-transfer.
Add a gentle S-curve of +15% contrast; keep shadows coloured and not black.
Keep the colour casts of mixed light; do not set a neutral white balance.
colour_and_grade.grain: Kodachrome 64: very fine, visible only at 40 × 50 cm

subject_and_staging.staging: None; the photographer uses the world as it is and the first frame is often the best.
subject_and_staging.direction: People are casual and look away, or are absent.

workflow: Process the slide film in E-6 or K-14 at standard time.
Make an 8×10 dye-transfer print from the slide or negative, with a deep, glossy surface.
Keep the print true to the film; make no local colour corrections.
post_processing.output: A glossy dye-transfer or chromogenic print at 30 × 40 cm with a dense, saturated surface.

canonical_works.work: Beverly Boulevard and La Brea Avenue, Los Angeles, California

emotion.target_response: Quiet delight in the ordinary: the viewer sees that a plain place has colour that a painter would envy.

avoid_when: The brief needs monochrome or a cinematic, graded look.
The scene is a controlled studio set.

modifiers.how: Switch to flat overcast light, set the camera level and frontal on a tripod, and desaturate by 60%; keep the plain subject.
Light and stage the scene, then grade shadows to teal and skin to orange; drop the casual composition.
